claims.statement: FDA identified that L-glutathione dietary-supplement powder labeled 'Caution: Dietary Supplement' was used by compounding pharmacies to make sterile injectable products despite the manufacturer stating it was not intended for sterile drug use; FDA laboratory testing found the material contained excessive bacterial endotoxin (up to five times the acceptable limit), and seven patients who received an injectable drug compounded with this L-glutathione experienced adverse events. This is not an isolated 2019 incident: FDA-documented endotoxin contamination in compounded glutathione injectables has recurred as recently as August 2026, when two separate Texas compounding pharmacies (Optimal Balance Pharmacy and Victory Medical Center Pharmacy) issued voluntary nationwide recalls of compounded glutathione 200 mg/mL multi-dose vials after pharmacy testing found elevated bacterial endotoxin levels and patients across at least 14 states reported adverse events including fever, chills, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, tachycardia, and blood-pressure changes.

claims.statement: In a randomized, double-blind, crossover pharmacokinetic study in 14 healthy adults, a 300 mg micellar glutathione formulation produced significantly higher systemic glutathione exposure and peak response than a standard 500 mg oral glutathione preparation (p=0.0064), and a 30-day, single-arm follow-up at 600 mg/day of the micellar formulation showed no significant change in liver enzymes (ALT, AST, ALP) or creatinine. This single small trial's own findings suggest, but do not by themselves establish, that standard (non-enhanced) oral glutathione has comparatively limited systemic absorption relative to the micellar formulation tested; no independent regulator-tier (A1/A2) source confirming this comparison has been identified, so the claim remains human-review-gated.

claims.statement: Glutathione is widely marketed online and at med-spas/IV-drip clinics as a 'master antioxidant' skin-lightening and 'detox' injection, but no published clinical trials evaluate injectable glutathione for skin lightening, and the only controlled human efficacy data identified in this packet involve oral glutathione at modest, only partially significant effect sizes; injectable/IV glutathione use for cosmetic or detox purposes accordingly lacks supporting controlled human efficacy evidence and is separately the subject of explicit regulatory safety warnings.
